LawProactive exists to make that first step easier. The attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover money for you. Whether your injury happened in a car accident on National City Boulevard, a fall, or another type of incident, reaching out costs nothing and starts the conversation about what comes next.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Sooner Rather Than Later

items.title: California's Filing Deadline
items.desc: Most injury claims in California must be filed within two years, but claims against a government entity can require notice in as little as six months. Waiting too long can mean losing your right to recover anything at all.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't Bar Recovery
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you're found partly responsible for a collision, you can still recover compensation reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no limit on compensation for pain, suffering, and other non-economic losses, unlike some other states.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no fee unless they win or settle your case. That means getting legal help doesn't add financial risk while you're already recovering.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in National City?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of the injury to file a personal injury lawsuit. If your claim involves a government entity, such as a city vehicle or defective public road, the notice period can be as short as six months, so it's worth checking your situation promptly.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, which means you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame for what happened. Your recovery would simply be reduced by your percentage of fault, not eliminated.

items.question: Where do collisions tend to cluster in National City?
items.answer: Public collision records show higher counts along corridors such as Highland Avenue, E Plaza Boulevard, National City Boulevard, and near the I-5 interchange, with reported crashes tending to peak on Wednesdays between 5 and 7 p.m. These are neutral public-record counts, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Do I have to pay anything to get connected with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and the independent attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if they recover compensation for you.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is not a law firm. We simply connect injured people in National City and throughout San Diego County with independent personal injury attorneys who can evaluate their situation.
